title: Comparing Your Real Options for Selling Courses Without Teachable or Stripe in 2025
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: If you're a creator in Nigeria, Ghana, or Pakistan, you've probably encountered the harsh reality of selling digital products without access to Stripe or Teachable. These platforms, while widely popular, impose strict restrictions on creators in certain countries, leaving them with limited options for selling their courses and other digital products. This is especially true for creators in countries hit by economic sanctions or currency fluctuations, like Nigeria, where the naira has struggled to maintain its value against the dollar.
What Each Option Actually Offers

The reality is that each platform has its own set of limitations and fees. Gumroad, for example, charges a flat 3.5% + 30¢ per sale, while Lemon Squeezy charges 0% + 20¢ per sale. PayPal, on the other hand, charges 2.9% + 30¢ per sale, but only for transactions under $10,000. Meanwhile, Stripe charges 2.9% + 30¢ per sale, with additional fees for international transactions. Teachable, if available, charges 0% + 10¢ per sale, but only for basic plans. These fees add up quickly, especially for creators who rely on digital sales to make a living.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

But what about creators in restricted countries? That's where things get even more complicated. Gumroad, while available globally, has inconsistent payment processing in certain countries, like Nigeria and Ghana. Lemon Squeezy, on the other hand, has a more restrictive approach, limiting access to creators in countries with high risk profiles. PayPal, despite its global presence, has a complex set of rules governing transactions in restricted countries, making it difficult for creators to navigate. Stripe, notoriously, has strict restrictions on creators in certain countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed and fees, things get even more convoluted. Gumroad, for example, takes 2-5 business days to process payments, while Lemon Squeezy takes 3-7 business days. PayPal, on the other hand, takes 2-3 business days to process payments, but only for transactions under $10,000. Stripe, notoriously, takes 2-5 business days to process payments, with additional fees for international transactions. Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The asymmetric risk of platform dependency becomes concrete only when the platform acts. While a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When it stops functioning — through suspension, policy change, or geographic restriction enforcement — the creator loses their revenue channel instantly, often with funds already inside the platform that cannot be withdrawn. The conventional appeals process rarely reverses these decisions because the original decision was made algorithmically and the human review process operates on the platform's timeline and criteria, not yours. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates this asymmetry entirely. Your Cloudflare Pages storefront cannot be suspended by a payment processor's compliance team. Your wallet cannot be frozen by anyone.
